records.description: A clean https image URL with no sensitive-looking query parameters is used directly as the displayable product image.
records.notes: imageUrl is resolved via normalizePersistedCommerceUrl (services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts:49-89), the same function backing the imageUrl/image_url/thumbnail/thumbnailUrl alias chain at :209-213. A plain https URL with no sensitive query keys, no /storage/v1/object/sign/ path segment, and no JWT-shaped path/query segment passes through unchanged.

records.description: When no image field is present at all, the product record must fail safely to a no-image/placeholder display state rather than rendering broken markup.
records.notes: SYNTHETIC: the data-layer resolution to null when imageUrl/image_url/thumbnail/thumbnailUrl are all absent is grounded in services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts:209-213 (each candidate passes through normalizePersistedCommerceUrl, which returns null for a non-string/undefined input). What this fixture actually asserts -- that the UI must render a safe placeholder/no-image state rather than broken markup -- describes a required behavior, not one inspected in a specific component in this lane, so no specific placeholder asset or component is claimed.

records.description: An image URL string that isn't a valid https URL is treated as absent, not displayed as broken markup.
records.notes: normalizePersistedCommerceUrl (services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts:49-51) requires the text to match /^https:\/\//i before it even attempts `new URL(...)`; a string with no https:// prefix returns null immediately, so it is resolved identically to an absent field.

records.description: An image URL carrying a long signed-token-shaped query string (?sig=...&expires=...) is actually REJECTED (resolved to null, treated as absent), not kept: the persisted image alias chain runs every image URL through the same normalizePersistedCommerceUrl() used for purchase-option destination URLs, and that function treats 'sig' and 'expires' as disqualifying query keys for ANY persisted commerce URL, image URLs included.
records.notes: JUDGMENT-CALL CORRECTION: the scenario was originally expected to be 'safe to keep' on the theory that no client-side helper is known to sanitize image URLs specifically. Direct inspection of services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts:11-30 (SENSITIVE_URL_QUERY_KEYS, an exact-match set including 'sig' and 'expires') and :49-89 (normalizePersistedCommerceUrl) shows one does exist and does reject this exact shape -- the same function backs the imageUrl/image_url/thumbnail/thumbnailUrl alias chain at :209-213 cited for img-multiple-fields-precedence, so it is the correct function to ground this scenario against. This is a real product-implication worth flagging: a legitimately signed/expiring CDN image URL would fail to persist through this path, not just a hostile one. No separate, more permissive image-URL-only sanitizer was found anywhere in source (a source gap: image URLs are not deliberately special-cased away from the destination-URL credential/signature checks, for better or worse).

records.description: When imageUrl, image_url, thumbnail, and thumbnailUrl are all present with different values, imageUrl wins: the alias chain tries imageUrl first and returns on the first non-empty normalized result.
records.notes: services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts:209-213: `normalizePersistedCommerceUrl(record.imageUrl) || normalizePersistedCommerceUrl(record.image_url) || normalizePersistedCommerceUrl(record.thumbnail) || normalizePersistedCommerceUrl(record.thumbnailUrl)` -- first non-empty normalized candidate wins, in that exact precedence order.

records.description: A valid-looking image URL that fails to load at render time (a runtime image-load event, not a URL-shape problem) must not crash the screen and must fall back to a safe empty/placeholder image state.
records.notes: SYNTHETIC boundary case; no specific image-load-failure handler (e.g. an <Image onError> handler) was located in source for this lane's research, so this describes required behavior, not observed behavior.
